points:
**(a) Convergent ends are extendible.** Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]) for the general absolutely continuous endpoint argument in this clause. Let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a future
causal curve and suppose $b:=\sup I<\infty$ and $\gamma(t)\to x\in M$ as
$t\to\sup I$. Then there is $\varepsilon>0$ and a future causal curve
$\tilde\gamma$ defined on $I\cup[b,b+\varepsilon)$ whose restriction to $I$
is $\gamma$. Consequently a future-inextendible causal curve whose domain is
bounded above does not converge at its upper end, and the dual statement
holds at the past end.

open $V$ with $p\in V\subseteq U$ there are a future causal curve
([[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]) $\sigma$ and parameters $s<t$ in
its domain with
$$\sigma(s),\sigma(t)\in V,\qquad \sigma([s,t])\not\subseteq V .$$
Then there exist an open set $W$ with $p\in W$ and $\overline W\subseteq U$
and, for every $k\ge2$, points $x_k,y_k\in W$ with $x_k\to p$ and
$y_k\to p$, together with future causal curves $\sigma_k:[0,1]\to M$ with
$\sigma_k(0)=x_k$, $\sigma_k(1)=y_k$ and
$$\sigma_k([0,1])\not\subseteq W .$$
No additional choice is used beyond these stated premises.

points:
Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Fix $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$, $\kappa>0$ and one smooth EOS $p=p(\epsilon)$ on an open interval $J$ with $\epsilon+p>0$ and $0<p'(\epsilon)<1$ ([[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]]). Let $\Sigma$ be a smooth three-manifold with smooth metric $h$, symmetric tensor $K_2$, density $\epsilon_0:\Sigma\to J$ and tangent field $v_0$ with $h(v_0,v_0)<1$. These specify the future unit initial velocity
$$U_0=W_0(N+v_0),\qquad W_0=(1-h(v_0,v_0))^{-1/2}$$
in $\mathcal V=\mathbb RN\oplus T\Sigma$, with metric $g_0(aN+X,bN+Y)=-ab+h(X,Y)$. Require the constraints of [[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]] for
$$T_0=(\epsilon_0+p(\epsilon_0))U_0^{\flat_{g_0}}\otimes U_0^{\flat_{g_0}}+p(\epsilon_0)g_0.$$
Then a smooth time-oriented local development has metric $g$, density $\epsilon$ and future unit fluid velocity $u$ satisfying
$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa\left[(\epsilon+p)u_au_b+pg_{ab}\right],\qquad D\epsilon+(\epsilon+p)\vartheta=0,\qquad (\epsilon+p)a^b+\Pi^{ba}\partial_ap=0.$$
Here $D=\nabla_u$, $\vartheta=\nabla_a u^a$, $a=\nabla_u u$ and $\Pi^{ab}=g^{ab}+u^au^b$. Initial geometric data are $(h,K_2)$ and initial matter data are $(\epsilon_0,U_0)$ under $N\mapsto n$, $X\mapsto i_*X$. Arbitrary smooth subluminal tilt is allowed. The initial surface lies in the interior of its intrinsic domain of dependence; its interior Cauchy neighborhood is globally hyperbolic. Any two developments of this same EOS and complete data agree near the entire initial surface by a data-fixing future isometry matching density and velocity. The neighborhood may have position-dependent time width; shocks, vacuum boundaries and vanishing sound speed are outside this strict interior-fluid statement ([[thm-gr-local-geometric-development]]).

points: Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]) and Dependent Choice ([[def-dependent-choice]]). Fix constants $c>0$, $\kappa>0$ and $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$. Let $\Sigma$ be a smooth three-manifold with smooth Riemannian metric $h$, smooth symmetric tensor $K$ and a smooth mass-normalized density $\rho_0\ge0$. Specify initial velocity as a smooth section $U_0$ of $\mathcal V=\mathbb RN\oplus T\Sigma$, with the bundle metric $g_0(aN+X,bN+Y)=-ab+h(X,Y)$, satisfying $g_0(U_0,U_0)=-1$ and positive $N$ coefficient. Thus the velocity need not be normal and does not presuppose a spacetime development. Put $\varepsilon_0=\rho_0c^2$ and require the constraints of [[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]] for $T_0=\varepsilon_0U_0^{\flat_{g_0}}\otimes U_0^{\flat_{g_0}}$. On $\{\rho_0>0\}$ this is exactly the dust supplier with density parameter $\varepsilon_0$, rather than $\rho_0$ ([[def-gr-dust-matter-model]]); zero regions have independently prescribed velocity.

Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Fix $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$, $\kappa>0$ and one scalar model $(\varphi,V,K_\phi)$ of [[def-gr-scalar-field-matter-model]], with its fixed smooth potential and normalization. Let $\Sigma$ be a smooth three-manifold with smooth Riemannian metric $h$, symmetric tensor $K_2$ and complete scalar data $(\varphi_0,\pi_0)$. Suppose the constraints of [[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]] hold for the scalar stress computed from these data, with $\pi_0$ the prescribed future-normal derivative. Then there is a smooth local Einstein-scalar development
$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa T_{ab},\qquad \Box_g\varphi-V'(\varphi)=0,$$
with induced geometric data $(h,K_2)$, $\varphi|_\Sigma=\varphi_0$ and $n(\varphi)|_\Sigma=\pi_0$. The neighborhood may have position-dependent time width. The initial surface is interior to its intrinsic domain of dependence; restricting to the interior Cauchy neighborhood gives a globally hyperbolic development. Every two developments of this same fixed model and complete data are related near the entire initial surface by a data-fixing time-orientation-preserving isometry matching $\varphi$. No potential positivity, mass sign, global existence or uniform noncompact slab is asserted ([[thm-gr-local-geometric-development]]).
